title: How to Break off an Engagement
treatment_title: How to break off an engagement.

location.name: The Abandoned Temple (Break Engagement node, Center zone)
location.kind: derelict seaside chapel on an eroding shore
location.real_analog: a storm-eaten island chapel in the Chesapeake Bay, like the lost church and graves of Holland Island, Maryland, swallowed by the water
near: side doors onto ivy and stone threshold

situation: No people: the tambourine thrown in Flashing Lights tumbles through black space and flies, still whole, through a chapel window. In time-lapse the empty chapel decays - choir stands, prayer lines, baptism pools, cobwebbed pews, gift boxes left outside the side doors - until a heavy storm takes over and speeds the decay. When the storm ends only remnants of the chapel are left on the shore, and the tambourine finally lands on them and shatters.
time_of_day: time-lapse across days or seasons, ending in storm and its aftermath
weather_light: dusty single-source interior light, then thunder, lightning and sheets of rain; after the storm a muted wet calm with one sunbeam breaking through (spine BE020)

set_pieces.name: Tambourine through the chapel window
set_pieces.what_happens: The tambourine falls, flies, tumbles through black space and enters the chapel through a window, still whole.
lines: a tambourine sounds off an / empty temple,
set_pieces.camera: tracking with the tumbling tambourine in black, then a clean pass through the window into the nave
set_pieces.position: a nave window on the chapel's seaward side (inferred side)

set_pieces.name: The empty temple
set_pieces.what_happens: Close-ups of an empty sanctuary in time-lapse decay: choir stands, kneelers, a dry baptism pool, pews veiled in cobwebs, ash drifting.
set_pieces.camera: locked-off time-lapse plates and macro close-ups on wood, stone and web

set_pieces.name: Gifts at the side doors
set_pieces.what_happens: Opened gift boxes left outside the side doors; spirits leave; ivy creeps over the cracked threshold.
lines: in opened gift / boxes placed / outside the side doors—
set_pieces.camera: low exterior angle on the threshold, time-lapse of boxes weathering
set_pieces.position: side doors and stone threshold, exterior

set_pieces.name: The storm
set_pieces.what_happens: Thunder; a heavy storm takes over and speeds the decay until nothing remains.
set_pieces.camera: wide exterior time-lapse of the chapel silhouette in lightning, pulling back as it is washed away
set_pieces.position: exterior, from the beach facing the chapel

set_pieces.name: Remnants on the shore
set_pieces.what_happens: Storm ends; what is left of the chapel lies on the shore with soaked bread, soiled blankets and footprints in mud.
lines: what was once love / now goods—
set_pieces.camera: still wides of wreckage at the tide line, inserts on bread, blanket and mud prints
set_pieces.position: the beach where the chapel stood

set_pieces.name: Tambourine shatters
set_pieces.what_happens: The tambourine finally lands on the ground of the chapel remnants and shatters.
set_pieces.camera: slow-motion ground-level impact, fragments scattering toward lens
set_pieces.position: on the chapel remnants at the shore

arrival.from_previous: The tambourine Young POET threw through his window tumbles through black space and flies into the chapel window, still whole. The POET does not appear.

departure.to_next: Cut to the POET standing on the same shore at night among the washed-up broken pieces (Nevermore).

encoding: The engagement is broken off in the building where it would have been sealed: a chapel stripped of choir, prayer and baptism, then erased by weather. Putting the temple on a shore lets the storm finish the job and leaves the pieces exactly where the poet will later walk - the ruin becomes the beach of the next poem. Inferred: the child's tambourine (the ode he was handed) survives the whole decay only to break last, so the breakup is completed by an object from his childhood.
